answer: An agent economy can require a staked history chain: each agent locks collateral and publishes signed receipts. Peers follow the thread of counterparties and trust only chains reaching a long horizon of distinct, bonded identities; any receipt that is a relic replayed from elsewhere is rejected. A Sybil farm cannot fabricate that past - it must pay staked agents to vouch for each clone, and if one link proves a duplicate, every voucher is slashed. Each extra fake identity costs fresh collateral and real prior work while its vote stays one, turning Sybils into a bill, not influence.
